page.text: YouTube often blocks or rate-limits server IP addresses. Routing yt-dlp and FFmpeg through a proxy keeps the playback working when the IP of your server gets flagged.

list.item: yt-dlp resolves the direct media URLs, without downloading anything.
FFmpeg downloads and decodes the stream from those URLs.

page.text: YouTube binds the resolved URLs to the IP address that requested them, so both steps must go through the same proxy.
page.syntax-highlight: PROXY = 'http://username:password@host:port' ... await app.play( chat_id, MediaStream( 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msiLgFkXvD8', ytdlp_parameters=f'--proxy {PROXY}', ffmpeg_parameters=f'-http_proxy {PROXY}', ), )
page.alert: FFmpeg only supports HTTP proxies. A SOCKS proxy passed only to yt-dlp is not enough, the download would come from a different IP address and fail.

subtext.text: Only yt-dlp is using the proxy, pass it to ffmpeg_parameters too.

subtext.category-title: HTTP Error 403 with a rotating proxy

subtext.text: The exit IP changed between yt-dlp and FFmpeg, use a sticky session.

subtext.category-title: Sign in to confirm you're not a bot

subtext.text: The proxy IP address is flagged, switch to a residential proxy or pass your cookies with --cookies cookies.txt.
Check the credentials and the format, it must be http://username:password@host:port.

page.text: PinguProxy sponsors PyTgCalls, the first 30 signups get 1GB for free. Two things matter when streaming:

list.item: Prefer residential proxies: YouTube flags datacenter IP ranges much more often, so they hit the bot check sooner.
Always use a session: rotating proxies change the exit IP on every connection, append _session-<id> to the username so yt-dlp and FFmpeg share the same IP address.

page.text: Port 12934 routes through residential IPs and 12933 through datacenter ones. A session per chat keeps every stream on its own IP, add _country-XX before the session to pick the exit country.
